details: District account identifies a shrine on the wooded hill, a square high tower, a smaller portico tower, a sixteen-column hall, dark granite and a roofed verandah.
1981 district census handbook repeats the granite details and classifies the smaller portico tower as circular.

Madras District Gazetteers: Vizagapatam (1907), pp.323–325. A terrace cut into the hill, square shrine and an enclosed verandah. The marriage hall outside the enclosure is identified by its 96 columns and the cited epigraphs establish several building dates.
Architecture section identifies the west-facing temple and five-tier Raja Gopuram with sculpture.
